screening_decisions.reason: This is a reporting guideline document (PRISMA extension), not a primary RCT investigating physical exercise in Parkinson's disease. It provides methodological guidance for reporting systematic reviews.

This is a randomized clinical trial evaluating dual-task aquatic exercises versus control in individuals with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control group.

This is a randomized controlled trial assessing progressive resistance exercise versus control in PD patients with akinesia-rigidity subtype. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control group.

This is a randomized cross-over trial evaluating a highly challenging balance exercise program versus usual care in PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control/usual care.

This is a single-blinded randomized trial comparing a 12-week community exercise program to control in PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control group.
This is a methodological paper describing a framework for assessing confidence in network meta-analysis results. Not a primary RCT investigating physical exercise in Parkinson's disease.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of Nordic walking studies, not a primary RCT. The review protocol specifies inclusion of RCTs only, not secondary literature.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two types of physical exercise (rebound therapy vs weight-supported exercises) in PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population, head-to-head comparison of exercise types.
This is a reporting guideline document (PRISMA statement), not a primary RCT investigating physical exercise in Parkinson's disease. Provides methodological guidance for systematic reviews.

This is a randomized controlled trial evaluating Baduanjin Qigong (a form of mind-body exercise) versus daily walking control in PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control group.

This is a randomized control trial comparing Argentine tango to self-directed exercise in PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention (dance), adult PD population, comparison to another exercise type.

This is a phase 2 multicenter randomized clinical trial comparing high-intensity treadmill exercise, moderate-intensity treadmill exercise, and wait-list control in de novo PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population, multiple comparisons including control.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of water-based exercise studies, not a primary RCT. The review protocol specifies inclusion of RCTs only, not secondary literature.

This is a randomized controlled trial evaluating multidisciplinary rehabilitation treatment (including aerobic and motor-cognitive components) versus no rehabilitation in PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise/rehabilitation intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control group.
This is a methodological paper describing the development of a quality-of-life measurement instrument (EuroQol). Not a primary RCT investigating physical exercise in Parkinson's disease.
This is an epidemiological study and meta-analysis examining gender ratios in PD prevalence/incidence. Not a primary RCT investigating physical exercise interventions in Parkinson's disease.

This is a pilot randomized controlled trial evaluating high-intensity aerobic cycling with balance training versus control in PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control group.

This is a pilot randomized controlled trial evaluating treadmill training versus lifestyle program control in PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, comparison to control group.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of dance practice studies, not a primary RCT. The review protocol specifies inclusion of RCTs only, not secondary literature.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing task-oriented circuit training combined with aerobic training versus aerobic training alone in PD patients. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population, head-to-head comparison of exercise types.

This is an RCT (60 patients randomized into 3 groups) comparing physical exercise interventions (treadmill gait training and conventional gait training) to a control group in patients with idiopathic PD. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a psychometric validation study of the Falls Efficacy Scale in community-living elderly persons, not an RCT. The population is not specifically PD patients, and there is no exercise intervention being tested.
This is a two-arm randomized controlled pilot study comparing two types of physical exercise (Tango argentino vs Tai Chi) in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a systematic review and network meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. While it includes RCTs in its analysis, the study itself is a review article.

This is a single-blind randomised crossover trial (153 patients) comparing a home physiotherapy programme based on rhythmical cueing (physical exercise intervention) to a control period in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a randomized, controlled, observer-blind crossover study comparing two types of physical exercise interventions (PMR plus visual cueing vs conventional physiotherapy) in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots. It is not an RCT, not focused on PD, and not about exercise interventions.
This is a randomized controlled single-blind trial comparing two types of physical exercise (Nordic Walking vs Walking) in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a review article summarizing diagnosis and treatment of Parkinson disease. It is not an RCT and does not test a specific exercise intervention.
This is a randomized clinical trial comparing progressive resistance training (physical exercise) to a control group (usual lifestyle) in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a meta-analysis of physiotherapy interventions in PD, not a primary RCT. While it includes RCTs in its analysis, the study itself is a review article.
This is a prospective cohort study examining test-retest reliability of outcome measures. It is not an RCT and does not test an exercise intervention.

This is a randomised controlled clinical trial comparing balance training (physical exercise) with different attentional focus instructions to a control group in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a randomized controlled pilot study comparing two types of physical exercise (water-based vs land-based exercise) in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT comparing Tai Chi training plus routine exercise to routine exercise alone in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria as it compares two types of physical exercise.
This is a single-center, parallel-group clinical trial comparing high-intensity tandem bicycle exercise (physical exercise) to a control group in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a systematic review of Tai Chi effects in PD, not a primary RCT. While it includes RCTs in its analysis, the study itself is a review article.
This is an RCT comparing power-based resistance training (physical exercise) to a control group in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT comparing two types of physical exercise interventions (yoga meditation vs proprioceptive training) in patients with PD. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a Cochrane systematic review of exercise for fall prevention in older community-dwelling people. It is not an RCT, and the population is not specifically PD patients (in fact, trials focused on particular conditions like PD were excluded).

This is a questionnaire validation study, not an RCT of physical exercise. The study focuses on developing and validating the PDQ-8 questionnaire as a shorter form of the PDQ-39. There is no physical exercise intervention or control group comparison.

This is an RCT comparing versatile physiotherapy intervention (physical exercise) to a control group in adults with PD. The study randomized 24 participants into intervention and control groups, with the intervention consisting of 16 one-hour therapy sessions based on European Physiotherapy Guidelines.

This is a cross-sectional observational study, not an RCT. The study examines the association between non-motor symptoms and quality of life in 411 PD patients. There is no physical exercise intervention or randomization.

This is an RCT comparing Health Qigong exercises (physical exercise) to a control group receiving only regular medication. Fifty-two PD patients were randomly divided into experimental and control groups, with the intervention lasting 12 weeks.

This is an RCT (Part Two) comparing walking training with verbal instructional cues (physical exercise) to a control group. Eleven individuals with PD were randomly assigned to treatment or control groups, with the intervention consisting of a 10-day training program.

This is an RCT comparing two types of physical exercise: Treadmill Training and Kinesiotherapy (TTK) versus Conventional Physiotherapy (CP). Twenty-four PD patients were randomly distributed into two groups, with both interventions being exercise-based.

This is an RCT comparing two different exercise programs: Agility Boot Camp (ABC) versus treadmill training. Participants were randomized into either exercise program, with both being physical exercise interventions.

This is an RCT (feasibility trial) comparing partnered ballroom dancing (physical exercise) to a control group receiving usual care. Fifty-one people with PD were randomized to control or experimental groups, with the intervention consisting of dance classes twice weekly for 10 weeks.

This is a network meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. The study synthesizes data from 19 existing studies to compare different exercise interventions. While it reviews exercise interventions, it is not itself an RCT.

This is an RCT comparing trunk resistance and stretching exercise (physical exercise) to a control group. Seventeen PD patients were randomly allocated into exercise and control groups, with the intervention lasting 12 weeks.

This is an RCT comparing power yoga (physical exercise) to a control group. Twenty-six patients with PD were randomly assigned to YOGA or control groups, with the intervention consisting of yoga classes twice weekly for three months.

This is an RCT comparing two exercise programs: combined balance and resistance training versus balance training only. Fifteen persons with PD were randomized into the two groups, with both interventions being physical exercise.

This is an RCT comparing leg muscle power training (physical exercise) to a control group receiving low intensity sham exercise. Community-dwelling people with PD were randomized, with both groups exercising twice weekly for 12 weeks.

This is an RCT comparing Tai Chi exercise (physical exercise) to control groups (placebo Qi-Gong or non-exercise). Forty-five participants with PD were randomly assigned to Tai Chi or control groups, with the intervention lasting 16 weeks.

This is an RCT comparing Sardinian folk dance (physical exercise) to usual care (control). Twenty individuals with PD were randomly assigned to the dance program or usual care, with the intervention consisting of dance sessions twice weekly for 12 weeks.

This is an RCT using a randomized delayed-start design comparing early start exercise program to delayed start (control). Thirty-one patients were randomized to early start or delayed start groups, with the intervention being a formal group exercise program.

This is an RCT comparing treadmill training (physical exercise) to a control group. Thirty-four patients with PD were randomized to speed TT, mixed TT, and control groups, with the intervention consisting of 72 one-hour exercise sessions over 24 weeks.

This is a consensus statement/methodology paper, not an RCT. The study proposes a standard set of outcome measures for PD through expert consensus. There is no physical exercise intervention or randomization.

This is a review article on the epidemiology of PD, not an RCT. The article reviews prevalence, incidence, risk factors, and prognosis from epidemiological studies. There is no physical exercise intervention or randomization.

This is an RCT comparing intensive rehabilitation treatment including aerobic exercise (physical exercise) to a control group receiving no therapy. Thirty participants with early-stage PD were randomly assigned to rehabilitation or control groups, with the intervention lasting 28 days.

This is an RCT comparing Nordic walking (physical exercise) to a control group in PD patients. The study randomly assigned 20 PD patients to NW group or control group, meeting the selection criteria for RCTs comparing physical exercise to control.

This is an RCT with 231 people with Parkinson disease randomized to exercise or usual-care control groups. The exercise targeted balance, leg strength, and freezing of gait, meeting the criteria for physical exercise intervention compared to control.

This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques (mixed treatment comparisons), not an RCT on physical exercise for PD. It discusses statistical methods for network meta-analysis, not a primary intervention study.

This is a randomised pilot study with 28 people with early PD randomized to immediate or delayed start of balance training. The intervention is a physical exercise (balance training) compared to delayed start control, meeting the selection criteria.

This study determines the minimal clinically relevant change for the FOG score measurement tool. It is not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions; it's a psychometric study about a measurement instrument.

This is an RCT with 22 PD patients randomized to experimental (slackline training) or control groups. Slackline training is a physical exercise intervention compared to control, meeting the selection criteria.

This study compares two different 12-week exercise programs (United Parkinson Foundation program and upper body karate training) in Parkinson patients matched for age, sex and stage. This is an RCT comparing one type of physical exercise to another type of exercise.

This is a methodological paper about network meta-analysis and treatment hierarchy questions. It is not an RCT on physical exercise for PD, but rather discusses statistical methodology for comparative effectiveness research.

This is an RCT with 22 PD patients randomized to three groups: aerobic training, strength training, and physiotherapy. This compares different types of physical exercise interventions, meeting the selection criteria.

This is a postal survey study determining minimally important differences for the PDQ-39 questionnaire. It is not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions; it's a psychometric study about a measurement tool.
This is a methodological paper about statistical approaches to multi-arm studies in network meta-analysis. It is not an RCT on physical exercise for PD, but rather discusses statistical methodology.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. The selection criteria specify RCTs, not reviews of RCTs. This study reviews 16 RCTs but is itself a secondary research article.

This is an open-label clinical trial, not a randomized controlled trial. The title explicitly states 'open-label' which indicates lack of randomization and blinding. The selection criteria require RCTs.

This is a pilot RCT with 20 PD patients allocated to exergaming group or conventional exercise control group. Exergaming is a physical exercise intervention compared to control, meeting the selection criteria.

This is an RCT with 40 PD patients randomly divided into water-based exercise group and land-based rehabilitation therapy group. This compares two types of physical exercise interventions, meeting the selection criteria.

This is an RCT with 51 people with early and midstage PD randomized to exercise intervention or usual care arm. The exercise program is a physical exercise intervention compared to control, meeting the selection criteria.

This is an RCT with participants allocated to Dance Group or Control Group (treatment as usual). Dance is a physical exercise intervention compared to control in early-stage PD patients, meeting the selection criteria.

This is a randomised waiting-list controlled trial with 32 adults with mild to moderate PD randomized to immediate gym training or delayed start. Gym training is a physical exercise intervention compared to waiting-list control, meeting the selection criteria.

This is an RCT with 41 PD patients randomly assigned to robot-assisted gait training or conventional physiotherapy. This compares two types of physical exercise/rehabilitation interventions, meeting the selection criteria.

This is a quasi-randomized pilot trial with 46 PD patients assigned to dance group, PD exercise group, or non-intervention group. While quasi-randomized rather than fully randomized, the study compares physical exercise (dance) to other exercise and control. Following the conservative approach (include when in doubt), this is included.
This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.
This study evaluates exercise intervention in PD with control/comparison groups. Design appears to be RCT or quasi-RCT.
This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.
This study evaluates exercise intervention in PD with control/comparison groups. Design appears to be RCT or quasi-RCT.
This is a clinico-pathological diagnostic accuracy study, not an RCT evaluating exercise interventions.
This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a cross-sectional analysis without intervention, not an RCT.
This study determines clinically important differences for measurement scales, not an exercise intervention trial.
This study evaluates exercise intervention in PD with control/comparison groups. Design appears to be RCT or quasi-RCT.
This is an epidemiological incidence study, not an intervention trial.
Does not meet selection criteria - either not an RCT, not focused on exercise intervention, or not in PD population.
This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.

This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.
This is an RCT evaluating physical exercise intervention in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria.
Does not meet selection criteria - either not an RCT, not focused on exercise intervention, or not in PD population.

Randomized crossover trial comparing Agility Boot Camp-Cognitive program vs Education in people with PD and freezing of gait. Measures motor outcomes (FoG, balance, dual-task cost). Meets RCT criteria with exercise intervention.

RCT randomly allocating PD patients to rehabilitation training program vs control group. Focuses on mobility, balance and gait exercises. Assesses motor outcomes including balance, gait, and physical performance.
RCT directly comparing physiotherapy vs general exercise in Hoehn Yahr stage II PD patients. Uses standard outcome measures (FIM, TUG, UPDRS). Clear comparison of two exercise types.

Feasibility RCT comparing Irish set dancing vs routine physiotherapy in mild to moderately severe PD. Assesses motor disability, balance, freezing of gait, and quality of life. Dance is a form of physical exercise.
Systematic analysis of epidemiological data on global burden of PD. Not an RCT, does not involve exercise intervention. Purely observational/epidemiological study.

Blind phase II RCT comparing trunk exercise plus falls prevention education vs education only in PD patients with falls history. Measures step-to-step symmetry, balance, mobility, and quality of life.
RCT comparing different treadmill training methods (partial body weight support vs auditory stimulus vs control) in PD patients. Assesses gait kinematics and quality of life.
RCT comparing body weight-supported treadmill training vs conventional physical therapy in PD patients. Long-term follow-up assesses ambulation speed and stride length improvements.
RCT comparing personalized home-based exercise program vs usual care in repeat fallers with PD. Primary outcomes include fall rates, balance measures, and quality of life.

Pilot RCT comparing three exercise modalities (functional training, bicycle exercise, exergaming) in elderly PD patients. All are physical exercise interventions measuring walking capacity and functionality.
Feasibility RCT evaluating best practice physiotherapy vs no physiotherapy in PD patients. While focused on feasibility, it is still an RCT design with exercise intervention and relevant outcomes.
RCT comparing VR-augmented balance training vs conventional balance training vs untrained control in PD patients. Both VR and conventional training are forms of physical exercise/balance training.

Study evaluating movement rehabilitation influence on motor symptoms in PD patients. Title suggests RCT design comparing physiotherapy intervention. Conservative approach to include pending full text review.
RCT comparing treadmill training vs nonintervention control in PD patients. Assesses functional lower-extremity tasks and exercise test parameters. Clear exercise intervention.
Feasibility RCT evaluating cueing exercise and education program for PD patients with freezing of gait. Includes exercise component targeting falls and gait improvement.
Animal study using 6-OHDA-treated rats. Not human participants, therefore does not meet inclusion criteria for adult humans with Parkinson's disease.
Single-blind RCT pilot study comparing water-based vs non-water-based physiotherapy in PD patients. Both are physical exercise interventions assessing postural deformities and motor outcomes.
RCT comparing VRWii exercise vs traditional exercise vs control in PD patients. Both exercise groups receive physical training targeting obstacle crossing and dynamic balance.
Systematic review and meta-analysis of existing RCTs. This is secondary literature, not a primary RCT. Does not meet inclusion criteria for original research.
RCT comparing three exercise modalities (multimodal, functional mobility, mental/leisure) in PD patients. All involve physical exercise components with cognitive/psychological outcomes.
This is a systematic review of 43 trials, not a primary RCT. The selection criteria require randomized controlled trials, not review articles.
This is an animal study using mice to investigate striatal circuit reorganization during skill learning. It does not involve human participants with Parkinson's disease and is not an RCT.

This is a methodological paper about ranking treatments in frequentist network meta-analysis. It discusses statistical methods using case studies in diabetes and depression, not an RCT on exercise for PD.

This is a mixed methods study focusing on qualitative exploration of participants' perceptions about exercise. While it references an RCT, the study itself is primarily qualitative/interview-based, not an RCT evaluating exercise effectiveness.
This is a methodological paper developing a taxonomy to classify fall-prevention interventions in older people. It is not an RCT and does not focus on Parkinson's disease specifically.

This is a randomized controlled trial with crossover design investigating physical therapy program in 68 patients with PD. It compares PT+medication vs medication alone, measuring UPDRS, mobility, and walking speed. Meets all selection criteria.

This is an RCT comparing yoga intervention (twice-weekly for 12 weeks) to usual routines in people with PD (n=26). Measures balance, LBP, and anxiety. Yoga is a physical exercise intervention meeting selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about imputing missing standard deviations in meta-analyses of antidepressant trials. Not an RCT on exercise for PD.

This is a randomized feasibility study comparing the Ronnie Gardiner Rhythm and Music Method to control in 18 PD patients. The RGRM method involves rhythm-based movement/rehabilitation which qualifies as physical exercise. Measures mobility, cognition, and QoL.
This is an epidemiological study of parkinsonism incidence and mortality over 13 years. It is observational, not an RCT, and does not evaluate exercise interventions.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. Additionally, the abstract content appears to discuss collective efficacy in Cambodian villages rather than mind-body exercises in PD, suggesting possible indexing error.

This is an RCT comparing progressive resistance training (twice weekly for 10 weeks) to non-contact control in 18 individuals with PD. Measures gait initiation performance. PRT is a physical exercise intervention meeting selection criteria.

This is an RCT comparing six-month brisk walking and balance exercise to active control (upper limb training) in 70 people with PD. Measures MDS-UPDRS motor score, gait, and balance. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a feature review integrating animal and human research on exercise-induced brain plasticity. It is not an RCT and focuses on Alzheimer's disease rather than Parkinson's disease.

This is an RCT comparing rhythmic auditory stimulation combined with intensive muscle strength training to rhythmic auditory stimulation alone in 86 elderly PD patients. Muscle strength training is a physical exercise intervention. Measures gait, balance, and ADL.

This is an RCT comparing movement strategy training to musculoskeletal exercises in hospitalized PD patients. Both arms involve physical interventions, with exercise therapy as one arm. Measures UPDRS, balance, walking speed, and QoL. Meets selection criteria.

This is an RCT comparing 12 weeks of twice-weekly aerobic exercise to non-exercising controls in 26 persons with early PD. Measures cardiorespiratory fitness, functional ability, and mood. Aerobic exercise is a physical exercise intervention meeting selection criteria.
This is a general overview/seminar article about Parkinson's disease covering epidemiology, genetics, diagnosis, and treatment. It is not an RCT and does not evaluate exercise interventions.

This is an RCT comparing downhill walking training to conventional therapy in 33 PD patients over 4 weeks. Measures gait parameters, thoracic kyphosis, and muscle strength. Downhill walking is a physical exercise intervention meeting selection criteria.

This is a single-blinded RCT comparing virtual reality rehabilitation to conventional physical therapy in 28 PD patients over 12 weeks. Measures balance and gait. Both interventions involve physical exercise elements, meeting selection criteria.
This study describes the development and validation of the PDQ-39 questionnaire, not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions.
This study constructs a self-report questionnaire for freezing of gait assessment, not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions.
RCT randomizing 40 PD patients to tai chi vs multimodal exercise training groups, comparing two types of physical exercise.
This study develops a balance measure for elderly individuals, not specifically PD patients, and is not an RCT on physical exercise.
Observational longitudinal study on socioeconomic burden of PD, not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions.
This study evaluates a functional mobility test for frail elderly, not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions in PD.
RCT randomizing 40 PD patients to resistance training vs balance training, comparing two types of physical exercise.
RCT randomizing 34 PD patients to hydrotherapy vs land-based rehabilitation, comparing two types of physical exercise.
Pilot RCT randomizing 17 PD patients to Qigong vs sham Qigong, comparing mind-body exercise intervention.
Methodological paper describing a risk of bias assessment tool, not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions.
Double-blind RCT randomizing 130 PD patients to home-based aerobic exercise vs stretching (active control), comparing two types of physical exercise.
RCT randomizing 62 PD patients to community-based tango program vs control (no intervention), comparing physical exercise to control.
Animal study using MPTP-lesioned mouse model, not an RCT in adult humans with PD.
Historical observational study on parkinsonism onset and progression, not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions.
RCT randomizing 32 PD patients to Turo (qigong dance) program vs waiting-list control, comparing physical exercise to control.
Questionnaire development study for measuring quality of life in PD, not an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions.
Controlled clinical study randomizing PD patients to behavioral treatment vs nonspecific psychological treatment, investigating effects on movement and posture.
RCT randomizing 40 PD patients to balance training vs resistance training, comparing two types of physical exercise.
Cluster-randomized trial comparing ParkinsonNet physiotherapy network care vs usual care for PD patients, involving structured physiotherapy interventions.
Study randomizing subjects including PD patients to tango classes vs traditional strength/flexibility exercise, comparing two types of physical exercise.
This is an observational population-based cohort study examining mortality predictors in parkinsonism/PD, not an RCT. No exercise intervention is studied.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of exercise therapies, not a primary RCT. Reviews are excluded per protocol which specifies inclusion of RCTs.

Randomized clinical trial with 64 PD patients assigned to high-intensity agility program vs no physical intervention control. Meets all criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population.
Randomized clinical trial with 45 PD patients in three groups (Nintendo Wii alone, conventional exercises alone, combined). Compares different types of physical exercise interventions in PD patients.
Randomized controlled trial with 48 PD participants randomized to exercise or control groups. Exercise program targeted leg muscle strength, balance, and freezing. Meets all inclusion criteria.
This describes a software tool (R package and web app) for visualizing risk-of-bias assessments. Not an RCT and not related to exercise intervention in PD.

12-week crossover randomized trial with 24 PD patients receiving interactive video game-based exercise training vs no exercise control. Video game-based exercise qualifies as physical exercise intervention.
This is a questionnaire development and validation study (PDQ-39). Not an RCT and does not involve exercise intervention.
Pilot randomized study with 20 PD patients assigned to Global Postural Reeducation (GPR) program vs control. GPR is a physical therapy/exercise intervention. Meets inclusion criteria.
Randomized controlled trial with 35 elderly PD patients assigned to 24-week resistance training program vs control. Resistance training is a physical exercise intervention.
Methodological paper describing network meta-analysis techniques using graph theory and electrical networks. Not an RCT and not about exercise intervention in PD.
Single-blinded randomized control trial with 76 PD patients receiving Tai Chi exercise vs no intervention control. Tai Chi is a physical exercise intervention meeting all criteria.

Prospective randomized controlled trial with 30 early PD patients randomized to high-intensity exercise, low-intensity exercise, or zero-intensity education control. Compares different exercise intensities.

While this is an RCT, the intervention is a group-based music intervention, not clearly a physical exercise intervention. Primary outcomes focus on dual-tasking, cognition, and mood rather than physical exercise effects.
Randomized pilot study with 40 newly diagnosed PD patients assigned to multidisciplinary intensive rehabilitation treatments (MIRT) vs drug-only control. MIRT includes physical exercise components.
Epidemiological burden of disease study analyzing neurological disorders in Europe. Not an RCT and not about exercise intervention.
Single-blind randomized controlled trial comparing PD-WEBB (weight-bearing exercise for better balance) training vs control in PD patients. Clear physical exercise intervention.
Randomized trial with 58 PD patients assigned to tango, waltz/foxtrot, or no intervention control. Dance is a physical exercise intervention. Compares different exercise types.
Randomized controlled crossover trial with 26 PD patients comparing aerobic training vs Qigong. Both are physical exercise interventions. Meets all criteria.
This is a Cochrane systematic review of physiotherapy interventions in PD, not a primary RCT. Reviews are excluded per protocol.

This is a randomized controlled trial (ensaio clínico randomizado) comparing two types of physical exercise (Nordic walking vs free walking) in people with Parkinson's disease. The study randomizes 33 subjects into two exercise groups and measures anthropometric outcomes. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a prospective, single-blind, randomized clinical trial comparing three groups: (1) multimodal balance training with rhythmical auditory stimuli, (2) regular multimodal balance training without auditory stimuli, and (3) control intervention (education program). 154 patients with PD were randomized. Meets all selection criteria for RCT comparing exercise interventions.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing incremental speed-dependent treadmill training (21 patients) vs control (10 patients) in patients with idiopathic Parkinson's disease. The study assesses postural instability, balance, and fear of falling. Meets all selection criteria.

This is a systematic review (Cochrane review) summarizing evidence from 8 trials about VR interventions for PD. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial itself, but rather a review of existing trials. Does not meet the selection criteria for primary RCTs.

This is a randomized controlled trial where 20 patients with PD were randomly divided into control and experimental groups. The experimental group performed a 4-week program of water-walking while executing dual-tasks. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing exercise intervention to control.

This is a randomized, controlled feasibility study with waiting list control. 20 people with idiopathic PD participated in a 12-week high-intensity interval training intervention. Assessors were blinded to group allocation. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing exercise to control.

This study describes gait analysis in parkinsonians after hydrotherapy programs. While it mentions '2 groups of patients underwent underwater or land based walking training', the abstract does not clearly state that this was a randomized controlled trial. The study design appears to be observational/comparative rather than an RCT. Excluded due to unclear randomization.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis examining 19 RCTs about physiotherapy for freezing of gait in PD. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial itself, but rather a review of existing trials. Does not meet the selection criteria for primary RCTs.

This is a comparative, prospective, randomized, single-blinded clinical trial comparing 3 types of physical exercise: (1) higher-intensity treadmill exercise, (2) lower-intensity treadmill exercise, and (3) stretching and resistance exercises. 67 patients with PD were randomly assigned. Meets all selection criteria for RCT comparing different exercise types.

This is a review article discussing pharmacological treatments (levodopa formulations, adenosine A2A antagonists, etc.) for motor fluctuations in PD. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not focus on physical exercise interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing Irish set dancing (1.5-hour class weekly for 10 weeks plus home program) vs usual care in 90 individuals with idiopathic PD. Dancing is a form of physical exercise. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing exercise intervention to control.

This is an observational cross-sectional study evaluating comorbidity of nonmotor symptoms (anxiety, depression, fatigue, sleep disturbance, sensory symptoms) in 99 PD patients. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not involve physical exercise interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.

The title indicates this study investigates Health Qigong exercises (a form of physical exercise) for treating PD symptoms. The abstract mentions 54 moderate PD patients. While the abstract is truncated, the title and partial abstract suggest this is likely an RCT comparing Qigong exercise intervention. Included conservatively pending full text review.

This is a randomized controlled trial with 210 people with PD randomized to 3 groups: (1) progressive resistance strength training with falls prevention education, (2) movement strategy training with falls prevention education, and (3) life-skills information (control). Both intervention groups involve physical exercise. Meets all selection criteria.

This is an open-label randomized controlled trial (ISRCTN26292510) comparing Ai Chi exercise (aquatic exercise) vs land-based exercise control in 40 patients with PD stages 2-3. Both groups involve physical exercise interventions. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing different exercise types.

This is a prospective, randomized controlled study comparing dance/movement therapy (10-week program) vs psychoeducational support group (control) in 13 patients with PD. Dance is a form of physical exercise. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing exercise intervention to control.

This is a randomized cross-over trial comparing a two-week physiotherapy programme with repetitive exercises of cueing and movement strategies vs no treatment in 22 patients with PD and freezing of gait. The intervention involves physical exercise. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing exercise intervention to control.

This is a pilot prospective single-blind, randomized clinical trial comparing multimodal balance training with rhythmical auditory stimuli vs without auditory cues in 35 patients with advanced PD (Hoehn & Yahr stage 4). Both groups involve physical exercise interventions. Meets selection criteria for RCT comparing different exercise types.

This is a review article providing an overview of the long-term effects of exercise and physical therapy in PD. It discusses evidence from previously published studies but is not itself a primary randomized controlled trial. Does not meet selection criteria for primary RCTs.

This is a secondary analysis of data from a large randomized controlled trial (154 patients with PD) comparing multimodal balance training with RAS vs without RAS vs control. While it is a secondary analysis, it analyzes data from an RCT comparing physical exercise interventions. Included conservatively as it provides RCT data on exercise interventions.
RCT comparing rehabilitation exercise intervention to routine care (control) in 200 hospitalized PD patients. Meets all criteria: RCT design, adult PD population, exercise vs control.
Pilot RCT comparing Tango, Waltz/Foxtrot, Tai Chi to No Intervention in 75 PD persons. Meets criteria: compares different exercise types to control group.
RCT comparing progressive resistance exercise to modified fitness counts program in PD patients. Meets all criteria: RCT, adult PD, compares two exercise types.
Pilot RCT randomly assigning 30 PD patients to Wuqinxi vs stretching groups. Meets criteria: RCT comparing two exercise types in adults with PD.
Neuropathology study examining neuronal loss patterns. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention, not a clinical trial. Does not meet selection criteria.
RCT comparing curved-walking training to control exercise in 24 PD subjects. Meets all criteria: RCT, adult PD, compares two exercise interventions.
Clinimetric validation study of rating scale. Not an exercise intervention trial, not an RCT comparing exercise types. Does not meet selection criteria.
Cross-sectional cohort study comparing cognitive performance between PD patients and healthy controls. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.
Prospective controlled trial comparing tango, treadmill walking, and stretching in 96 PD participants. Meets criteria: controlled trial, adult PD, compares multiple exercise types.
Review article on epidemiology and risk factors. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention trial. Does not meet selection criteria.

RCT comparing adapted resistance training with instability to traditional motor rehabilitation in PD patients with freezing of gait. Meets all criteria: RCT, adult PD, compares two exercise interventions.
RCT comparing aerobic exercise to goal-based exercise and control in 76 PD individuals. Meets all criteria: RCT, adult PD, compares exercise types to control.
RCT comparing balance training to general physical exercises in 64 PD patients with postural instability. Meets all criteria: RCT, adult PD, compares two exercise types.
RCT with random allocation to control and two exercise groups (with/without balance pad). Meets criteria: RCT, adult PD, compares exercise interventions to control.
Randomized controlled pilot trial comparing aquatic therapy to land-based therapy in 11 PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT, adult PD, compares two exercise/therapy types.
RCT comparing Nordic walking to free walking in 33 PD patients. Meets all criteria: RCT, adult PD, compares two exercise types.

RCT comparing intensive rehabilitation treatment (treadmill and stabilometric platform training) to pharmacological treatment with generic home exercise in 50 PD patients. Meets criteria: RCT, adult PD, exercise intervention vs control.
RCT comparing mindfulness yoga to stretching and resistance training in 187 PD patients. Meets all criteria: RCT, adult PD, compares two exercise types.
Review article about deep brain stimulation. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.
Clinical diagnostic criteria document. Not an RCT, no exercise intervention. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing gait and step perturbation training (physical exercise intervention) to a control group in adults with Parkinson's disease. The study meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and comparison to control.

This is NOT a randomized controlled trial. It is a reliability study of a questionnaire (NFOG-Q) comparing patient and carer ratings. There is no physical exercise intervention being tested. Does not meet the RCT selection criteria.

This is a randomized single-blind controlled trial comparing three exercise interventions (treadmill with music, treadmill without music, home walking) in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population, and comparison between exercise types.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing three exercise interventions (LSVT BIG, Nordic Walking, domestic nonsupervised exercises) in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population, and comparison between exercise types.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing three exercise/physiotherapy interventions (LSVT BIG, intensive physiotherapy, conventional physiotherapy) in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population, and comparison between exercise types.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing two rehabilitation/exercise interventions (VR rehabilitation vs conventional rehabilitation) in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise/rehabilitation interventions, adult PD population, and comparison between exercise types.

This is a randomized crossover trial comparing two exercise interventions (body weight-supported treadmill training vs conventional physical therapy) in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design (crossover), physical exercise interventions, adult PD population, and comparison between exercise types.

This is a quasi-randomized trial comparing exercise therapy to control (pharmacological therapy only) in adults with Parkinson's disease. While not a true RCT, it is close to meeting criteria and tests a physical exercise intervention. Following conservative screening guidelines, this study is included for further review.

This is a randomized controlled pilot trial comparing home-based treadmill training (physical exercise intervention) to usual care in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and comparison to control.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing dance therapy (a form of physical exercise/movement intervention) to a support group in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and comparison to control.

This is a 16-month randomized controlled trial comparing three exercise interventions (flexibility/balance/function exercise, supervised aerobic exercise, home-based exercise) in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise interventions, adult PD population, and comparison between exercise types.

This is NOT a randomized controlled trial. It is a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs. The selection criteria specifically require RCTs, not review articles. Does not meet the study design criteria.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing a home exercise program (strength training, movement strategy training, falls education) to non-specific life skills training in adults with Parkinson's disease. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, physical exercise intervention, adult PD population, and comparison to control.
